
  ▲ vercel env update name [options]

  Update the value of an existing Environment Variable (see examples below)     

  Options:

  -e,  --environment <ENVIRONMENT>  Pick the variable to update by an           
                                    environment it covers. The new value applies
                                    to all of its environments                  
       --git-branch <BRANCH>        Pick the variable to update by its Git      
                                    branch                                      
       --project <NAME_OR_ID>       Project name or ID (default: linked project)
       --sensitive                  Store the updated value as a Secret         
       --type <TYPE>                Set the Environment Variable type (`config` 
                                    or `secret`)                                
       --value <VALUE>              New value for the variable                  
                                    (non-interactive). Otherwise use stdin or   
                                    you will be prompted.                       
  -y,  --yes                        Skip the confirmation prompt when updating  
                                    an Environment Variable                     


  Global Options:

       --cwd <DIR>            Sets the current working directory for a single   
                              run of a command                                  
  -d,  --debug                Debug mode (default: off)                         
  -Q,  --global-config <DIR>  Path to the global `.vercel` directory            
  -h,  --help                 Output usage information                          
  -A,  --local-config <FILE>  Path to the local `vercel.json` file              
       --no-color             No color mode (default: off)                      
       --non-interactive      Run without interactive prompts (default: on when 
                              an agent is detected)                             
  -S,  --scope                Set a custom scope                                
  -t,  --token <TOKEN>        Login token                                       
  -v,  --version              Output the version number                         


  Examples:

  - Update a variable in all Environments

    $ vercel env update <name>
    $ vercel env update API_TOKEN

  - Update the variable that covers a specific Environment

    $ vercel env update <name> --environment <production | preview | development>
    $ vercel env update DB_PASS --environment production

  - Update the variable for a specific Environment and Git Branch

    $ vercel env update <name> --environment <production | preview | development> --git-branch <BRANCH>
    $ vercel env update NPM_RC --environment preview --git-branch feat1

  - Update a variable from stdin

    $ cat <file> | vercel env update <name> --environment <production | preview | development>
    $ cat ~/.npmrc | vercel env update NPM_RC --environment preview
    $ vercel env update API_URL --environment production < url.txt
